name: Atlassian and Bitbucket audit dashboard
summary: Four-tab Graylog dashboard for the audit data this exporter ships: access and permission changes, Bitbucket activity, data movement, feed health
description:
A dashboard for the Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket audit records produced by atlassian_log_exporter, shipped to Graylog over GELF.

Tabs:
  * Access and permissions - group membership changes over time, most-changed groups, privileged configuration changes (group/space create and delete, permission and role changes), and a detail table of who was added or removed and to which group.
  * Bitbucket - repository activity over time, by repository, by author, and the action-type mix.
  * Data movement - Confluence site exports and who ran them, content restrictions added, and attribution coverage by category.
  * Feed health - messages per day by source and the newest audit events, so a stalled exporter is visible rather than silent.

IMPORTANT, and the reason the 'attribution coverage' panel exists: the Jira and Confluence audit log records the ACTOR as the Jira/Confluence application itself for group and user management events. The panels therefore show WHAT changed and TO WHOM, but not who made the change. That is a limitation of the audit log available without Atlassian Guard, not of the exporter or of these queries - verified across the full retained history. Bitbucket commit records DO carry an author.

All queries key on `source` (jira, confluence, bitbucket-commits) and the `summary` field, so nothing here is specific to one Atlassian site.
